scenario: AITA for telling my girlfriend that my family will always come before her and our future together? | My girlfriend expects me to build a future for us. A little back story: She's a student right now and works part time but barely makes enough to pay her rent/school fees. I'm 24 and work a minimum wage + commission job, I have barely any money saved so she doesn't understand why I spend so much money/time with family We've been dating 3 years with no problems except for this, we love each other and live independent lives but she worries that I'm too focused on helping my family and making them happy instead of building a future for us. She's working as much as she can to pay her bills but because shes a student and also doing her required interning she can't work much more. She doesnt ever ask me for money to help her right now because she wants me to save up. She doesn't have a family like mine so she doesn't understand, my family is close and I really want to take care of them. She says that I'm supposed to be worrying about my own future right now. She says that she doesn't understand because my mom recently received about ~100k for a settlement and bought a house and a new car and I shouldn't be worrying about helping when they seem fine. She is angry that I dont take my life seriously, I've been trying to get my real estate license for a few months now but cant find the time to study because of how demanding my family is, they get really angry/sad when I'm not around for family events and I understand why, we're a close family. I get where shes coming from but I cant drop my family. I told her all of this and she got angry saying that shes not asking me to abandon my family, she just wants to make sure we have a solid foundation before we worry about helping my family. And I cant build a future if I'm always with them. She expects me to start saving up money for a downpayment on a house while she finishes and gets her degree and can start helping as well but I keep telling her my family needs me first. We had a particularly heated fight, the worst we've ever had last night and she said she feels like I'll never care enough about my future and I'm supposed to be building one for myself and her and she can't be with someone like that. She said if I really feel like helping my family comes before my own future than that is my choice but she's going to have no choice but to worry about herself from now on and plan a future where shes her only priority because I make it sound like I don't want to be part of it. Shes stopped mentioning anything about it and is now talking about saving up for a one bedroom apartment and a car for herself (she lives in a basement). She seems so sad but I cant help but feel like shes wrong for even asking me to not help my family. I dont know if I'm being an asshole or not for telling her that my family will always come first. AITA for telling her my family and their needs have to come before her and our future together?

Let me start by understanding the situation better. I'm a 24-year-old man working a minimum wage plus commission job, which doesn't leave me with much savings. My girlfriend is a student working part-time, barely making enough to cover her rent and school fees. She's really focused on building a future for us, but I've been spending a lot of time and money helping my family. We've been dating for three years without any major issues except this. My family is very close, and I feel a strong responsibility to take care of them. Recently, my mom received a settlement of about $100k, bought a house, and a new car. Despite this, I still feel the need to help them, which my girlfriend doesn't understand. She thinks I should be focusing more on my own future, like getting my real estate license, which I've been trying to do but can't find the time because of family demands. We had a really heated fight about this, and she's now talking about saving up for her own place and car, feeling like she can't rely on me for the future. She's sad, and I'm left wondering if I'm being an asshole by prioritizing my family over her. So, is it right or wrong to tell her that my family comes first? Let me break this down. First, I need to consider the importance of family versus a romantic relationship. Families are often considered a primary source of support, and many people feel a deep obligation to help them. On the other hand, a romantic partner is someone you build a future with, and they might expect similar dedication. I also need to think about communication. Did I explain my reasons clearly? It seems like I did, but she still feels hurt and unsupported. Maybe there's a way to balance both responsibilities. Another point is the practical aspect. If I'm not saving money for our future because I'm helping my family, that could create financial strain. My girlfriend is trying to save on her own, but she's still a student with limited income. She might feel that I'm not contributing as much as she needs. I also wonder about the long-term implications. If I continue to prioritize my family, could that lead to resentment in the relationship? Or could it strengthen our bond if we find a way to support each other? Maybe I should consider setting boundaries. Is there a way to help my family without neglecting my relationship? Perhaps by finding a balance or discussing expectations with both my family and my girlfriend. I also need to reflect on whether my family's needs are as urgent as I perceive them. My mom has a settlement, so maybe they're more stable than I think. Could I be overestimating their need for my help? In terms of personal values, I value loyalty and taking care of my family, which is important. But I also value my relationship with my girlfriend, and I don't want to lose that. Finding a middle ground might be the key. I should also think about the future. If I don't start saving for a down payment or focus on my career, will that affect our ability to build a life together? My girlfriend is working towards her degree, which is a good step, but I need to contribute as well. Perhaps I can talk to my family about my need to focus on my own future. Maybe they can understand that while I love them, I also need to prioritize my own life and relationship. It might be a tough conversation, but it could help alleviate some of the pressure I'm feeling. On the flip side, my girlfriend might not fully understand the depth of my family obligations, especially if she doesn't have a similar family structure. She might feel neglected or unsupported, which is valid. I need to acknowledge her feelings and find a way to make her feel valued despite my family commitments. In conclusion, while it's important to support family, it's equally important to nurture a romantic relationship. Finding a balance where both my family and my girlfriend feel supported might be the solution. I need to communicate openly, set realistic expectations, and perhaps adjust my priorities to ensure both aspects of my life are addressed.
